chunk_findings.detail: `delta_note` joins `h.delta` onto `DELTA_DIR` and treats any non-empty read as a recorded gap. `Path` replaces the base when the right-hand side is absolute, and `..` is honored by `read_text`, so the check is not confined to `templates/drivers/deltas`. A bespoke harness with `delta="/etc/hostname"` (or `delta="../some-nonempty.txt"`) and `recorded={"novel"}` makes `unrecorded` return `[]` even though no driver delta note exists; the ratchet the change adds is bypassed by the path in the descriptor field, not by a note that states the gap and its reason.

data.claim: The R-orchestrators-2026-11-09 fields -- model_visibility (visible|hidden|unknown), cost_exposed (per_run|per_turn|none|unknown), subagent_model_control (per_spawn|per_file|env|none|unknown) and patterns (router|planner_executor|subagents|best_of_n|council) plus the file and key that set each -- are a [capabilities] descriptor v2 section; a verified value must cite its *_source, unverified stays unknown.
data.falsifier: A descriptor declaring model_visibility='visible' with NO source parses (a guessed value): then the never-guessed ratchet is absent.
data.mechanism: harnessv2 owns the record + closed vocabularies; harnessreg stores [capabilities] on the descriptor; check_table rejects an out-of-vocabulary value and validate rejects a non-unknown value whose *_source is empty.
data.probe: HR.parse(grok.toml + '[capabilities] model_visibility="visible"') raises DescriptorError naming model_visibility_source; with a source it parses.
data.probe_output: refused: grok.toml: capabilities.model_visibility is 'visible' but capabilities.model_visibility_source names no file and key; with source -> parses, verified={model_visibility}; 7 tests pass.
data.question: Which orchestration capabilities matter per harness, and are they descriptor data graded by validation (a verified value cites its source, unverified stays unknown) rather than guessed?

evidence.note: Filed research R33c76842eb CONFIRMED: [capabilities] section (model_visibility/cost_exposed/subagent_model_control/patterns + *_source), verified value cites source, unverified stays unknown; probe HR.parse refuses a sourced-absent 'visible'.

Read rules digest; reused the descriptor v2 + harnessreg parse + harnessv2 vocabularies (never a second state machine); no live model calls. Followed the v2 reservation contract (own the section here once).

Added [capabilities] section (harnessv2.Capabilities + vocab + validation), harnessreg Harness.capabilities, parity/orchestration.py report (record/verified/report), catalog.toml 4 rows + history; tests/test_parity_orchestration.py 7 tests. Committed 67d4cbfc3. ruff clean.

chunk_findings.detail:
The source guard only checks truthiness, so a verified non-`unknown` capability can pass with a meaningless source. For example, a TOML descriptor containing:
```toml
[capabilities]
model_visibility = "visible"
model_visibility_source = " "
```
passes because `not " "` is false, so no `DescriptorError` is raised. That lets a row claim `visible` (or `per_run`, `per_spawn`, patterns, etc.) while citing no actual file/key, defeating the stated falsifier that visible/exposed values must cite a real source.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/harnessv2.py:357 (`capabilities` source validation)

chunk_findings.detail:
The membership test `p in PATTERNS` assumes every list element is hashable. Given TOML input:
```toml
[capabilities]
patterns = ["router", ["council"]]
patterns_source = "x"
```
`patterns` is a list, but evaluating `["council"] in PATTERNS` raises `TypeError: unhashable type: 'list'` instead of the intended `DescriptorError`. Malformed configuration crashes validation rather than being reported as invalid.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/harnessv2.py:270 (`capabilities.patterns` validation)

chunk_findings.detail: The changed source guard now calls `source.strip()` (and `cap.patterns_source.strip()` at line 363) without first checking that the source value is a string. A TOML descriptor can provide a non-string source such as `model_visibility_source = []` or `model_visibility_source = true`; the capabilities validation shown only type-checks `patterns` elements, so the raw non-string value reaches this line and raises `AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'strip'` instead of the intended `DescriptorError`. The previous `not source` guard would reject an empty list/None as “no source,” so this edit turns malformed descriptor validation into a crash.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/harnessv2.py:358

chunk_findings.detail: `verified` marks a capability as verified from the value alone and never inspects the corresponding `*_source`. Given a capabilities record such as `model_visibility="visible"`, `cost_exposed="unknown"`, `subagent_model_control="unknown"`, `patterns=()`, with `model_visibility_source` missing or empty, `report` returns `"verified": ["model_visibility"]`. That reports a visible-model row with no source/check, which is exactly the stated falsifier; the same applies to `patterns=("subagents",)` without a non-empty patterns source. The function should require the matching source field to be present/non-empty, not merely require the value to be non-unknown.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/parity/orchestration.py:34

chunk_findings.detail: The new source validation calls `source.strip()` without checking that `source` is a string. Given a TOML descriptor such as `[capabilities] model_visibility = "visible"` and `model_visibility_source = 1` (or `true`), `_validate_section` validates `model_visibility` but not the source field, so a `Capabilities` object is constructed with `model_visibility_source=1`. `_validate_descriptor` then raises `AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute 'strip'` instead of a `DescriptorError`. The same applies to `patterns_source` when `patterns` is non-empty, e.g. `patterns = ["router"]` with `patterns_source = 1`. Malformed descriptor data should be rejected by the descriptor validator, not crash with an unrelated Python exception.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/harnessv2.py:358

chunk_findings.detail: The new PAR-catalog rows claim to add orchestration capability fields, but every row sets `descriptor_fields = []`. The only descriptor field introduced by the change is `HarnessDescriptor.capabilities` (`ddflow/services/harnessreg.py:225`), and no catalog row names it or any of the capability fields described in the notes. A catalog consumer that uses `descriptor_fields` to map descriptor fields to catalogued features will therefore see a descriptor with a `[capabilities]` section as not covered by any feature, so the fields are not actually added to the feature catalogue despite the notes saying they are graded by descriptor validation.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/harnesses/catalog.toml:194

chunk_findings.detail: The new source checks assume every `*_source` field is a string. For a descriptor such as `[capabilities] model_visibility = "visible" model_visibility_source = 1` (or `patterns = ["router"] patterns_source = ["settings.json", "patterns"]`), the membership validation accepts the scalar value, the `Capabilities` instance stores the non-string source, and then `source.strip()` / `cap.patterns_source.strip()` raises `AttributeError` instead of a `DescriptorError`. A malformed descriptor should fail validation cleanly, not crash the validation path.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/harnessv2.py: capabilities source enforcement

chunk_findings.detail: `verified` marks a capability as VERIFIED whenever the value is not `unknown` and the corresponding `*_source` is any non-whitespace string; it never requires the source to be a file/key citation and never requires an offline check. For example, a descriptor record such as `HV.Capabilities(model_visibility="visible", model_visibility_source="source")` causes `verified` to return `{"model_visibility"}` even though no file/key source and no offline check are cited. If a `*_check` field exists, an empty/missing check is ignored here as well. This can make `report` list a field as verified when the survey rule requires both a source and an offline check, and it contradicts the change’s stated falsifier that a visible/exposed field without proper verification is wrong.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/parity/orchestration.py:verified

chunk_findings.detail: The report test does not enforce the “never guessed” property it claims. For a descriptor with no source or offline check, an `ORC.report()` entry such as `{"grok": {"model_visibility": "visible", "cost_exposed": "per_run", "subagent_model_control": "per_spawn", "patterns": ["evergreen"], "verified": ["model_visibility"]}}` passes all assertions: `set(entry["verified"])` is still a subset of the four field names, each scalar value is in its vocabulary constant, and the test never checks that non-`unknown` values have a source/check or that `patterns` are valid patterns. Thus the test can pass even when the report asserts a visible/exposed capability with no source, which is exactly the falsifier.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_parity_orchestration.py:test_the_report_grades_every_descriptor_without_guessing

chunk_findings.detail: The new `capabilities` check decides that a capability is “VERIFIED” solely from the value being non-empty/non-`unknown`; it never inspects the paired `*_source` fields. For example, a descriptor that parses as `Capabilities(model_visibility="visible", model_visibility_source="")` (a shape the orchestration report treats as unverified) makes `driver_conformance.run` emit `checks["capabilities"] = {"status": "ok", "detail": "model_visibility"}`. Because the new catalog rows for model-visibility, cost-exposed, subagent-model-control, and patterns all list `checks = ["capabilities"]`, any consumer that treats an ok check as the row’s offline verification will accept a visible/exposed capability with no cited source, contrary to the stated falsifier that a row must not say visible/exposed without a source/check.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/driver_conformance.py:capabilities check

chunk_findings.detail: The new `capabilities` check, which catalog rows now cite as their offline check, always returns `status: "ok"` and lists a field as soon as its value is not `""` or `"unknown"`. It never reads `*_source` and never consults `verified()`. Given `HV.Capabilities(model_visibility="visible")` (or `model_visibility_source=""` / whitespace) with the other fields unknown, the emitted detail is `"model_visibility"` while the comment claims that list is what the descriptor declares VERIFIED and nothing guessed. That is the survey falsifier: a non-unknown value with no source is reported as a passing, verified capability. The same input is the case the prior probe said `verified()` leaves unverified, so this check and that grader disagree.

evidence.note: Derived the per-row answer in facts.STATUSES over the catalog rows: grok -> {verified:16, unverified:10, none:4}; a declared section reads verified, none=true reads none, absent reads unverified, a no-field row reads none.
Reused facts.STATUSES (verified/documented/unverified/none) + harnessreg sections + catalog rows + facts.best; did not invent a second state machine. No live calls.
Added ddflow/services/parity/answers.py (answer/answers/unanswered, derived, total) + tests/test_parity_answers.py (5 tests). Committed 69c35d63a. ruff clean.

chunk_findings.detail: `answer` treats an empty `descriptor_fields` list as a valid not-applicable answer (`"none"`), and `unanswered` only looks for statuses outside `facts.STATUSES`. Thus a catalog row that is simply unmapped or has a typoed/empty `descriptor_fields` (for example `row.feature="new-knob", row.descriptor_fields=[]`) is silently answered as `"none"`, `answers(h)` includes it, and `unanswered(h)` returns `[]`; the intended lint failure for an unanswered row cannot occur. This guesses not-applicable rather than marking the row unverified/unanswered.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/parity/answers.py:answer/unanswered

chunk_findings.detail: The code derives `sections` from only the text before the first dot and then checks only that top-level harness attribute. Given a row whose descriptor field is a dotted path such as `descriptor_fields=["mcp.servers"]`, if the harness has an `mcp` section but the descriptor does not declare `servers`, `answer` still appends `{"s": "verified"}` and returns `verified`. The row is reported supported even though the named field is absent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/parity/answers.py:answer

chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/parity/answers.py:answer

chunk_findings.detail: `answer` treats every falsy `row.descriptor_fields` as a documented “not applicable” answer by returning `"none"`. The docstring itself says not-applicable is `descriptor_fields` empty *plus a note/documented gap*, but the code never checks the note, gap flag, or any loader-provided reason. Given an active catalog row with `descriptor_fields=[]` and no documented gap (i.e. a row whose descriptor field is simply unknown), `answer` returns `"none"`, `unanswered` omits it because `"none"` is a valid `facts.STATUSES` value, and harness lint passes. That silently converts an unverified row into a documented non-applicable row, violating “marking the rest unverified, never guessed.”
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/parity/answers.py:21

chunk_findings.detail: The derivation collapses documented absence and not applicable into the same `"none"` status and discards the reason. A section record with `none = true` (documented absence) and a row with empty `descriptor_fields` (documented ddflow-side knob) both produce `answer(...) == "none"`, and `answer` returns only a string, so the section’s reason/note is dropped. The change’s stated contract requires four distinguishable answers — supported, documented absent, unverified, and not applicable with a reason — and says to reuse the facts states; this implementation never uses the `documented` state and provides no reason, so lint/conformance cannot distinguish a documented absence from a documented not-applicable row.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/parity/answers.py:29

chunk_findings.detail: A declared section is graded `verified` even though nothing was verified. `answer` only looks at `getattr(h, name)` and `record.none`; given grok’s `[mcp]` block and catalog row `mcp-config`, it returns `verified` (the new test locks that in). `facts` still has a distinct `documented` state, which this grader never emits. Declaration is not evidence, and the change forbids live checks, so the row is documented at best. Callers that treat `verified` as checked support will over-claim every backfilled descriptor.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/parity/answers.py:33

chunk_findings.detail: Not-applicable and documented-absent are the same status, and the reason is dropped. A catalog row with empty `descriptor_fields` (the tests’ `lean-tool-profile` / `key-by-env-name`, which are ddflow-side knobs, not harness absences) returns the bare string `"none"`, identical to a section with `none=true`. The required “not applicable with a reason” is not in the `dict[str, str]` result, so a report cannot tell “does not apply” from “documented unsupported”.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/parity/answers.py:22

chunk_findings.detail: Multi-section rows are collapsed with `facts.best`, which cannot implement the stated rule. For `descriptor_fields` naming both `mcp` and `capabilities` on grok (mcp present, capabilities missing), `have` is `verified` plus `unverified`. Whichever single status `best` returns is wrong: `verified` marks the row supported while a named section is absent; `unverified` denies the section that is declared; `none` invents a documented absence. Support has to be the conjunction of the named sections, not the best single fact.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/parity/answers.py:24

chunk_findings.detail: The lint failure this change promises cannot fire. `unanswered` keeps only statuses outside `facts.STATUSES`, but every path in `answer` returns `verified`, `unverified`, `none`, or `facts.best(...)["s"]` — all in that set — including a descriptor that declares nothing and a row whose fields failed to load (empty `descriptor_fields` becomes `none`, not unanswered). The change also never calls `unanswered` from harness lint, so an unanswered row is not failed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/parity/answers.py:42
